descriptionChirho: A spoken word, utterance, or saying, emphasizing the content of speech as a discrete communicative unit. In singular form it denotes a specific word or statement: 'every word that proceeds from the mouth of God' (Matt 4:4/Luke 4:4), 'the word of the Lord' coming to John (Luke 3:2), Mary's acceptance of the angel's word (Luke 1:38), the word of Jesus that Peter remembered (Matt 26:75), or a legal matter established by witnesses (Matt 18:16). In plural it refers to collections of spoken words or sayings: Jesus's words (John 6:63, 6:68, 8:20, 8:47), the words of the prophets (Acts 2:14), and words remembered or reported (Luke 1:65, 2:19, 24:8). The singular 'matter/thing' nuance (as in Acts 5:32) represents the common Semitic extension of 'word' to 'thing/matter' (cf. Hebrew dabar), not a genuinely separate sense. All clusters represent the same fundamental meaning across number and contextual variation.
